title: Have you had success with chinese models? Whats the best alternative you tried? For making and designing games.
author: Prior-Meeting1645
selftext: Its got to have vision right? And the biggest vision model is kimi I believe?

comments.author: yapdakilla81
comments.body: GLM 5.1 and Deepseek. I dont need vision. Shipped a game Mycelium Conquest on Steam using them

replies.author: lostforever2011
replies.body: Maybe you can help, i can code game easily with LLM, my issues always have been art assets. I don't know how to use LLM to generate art assets.  Can you point me towards how to so that pleases? Maybe even some explanation as to how you did that? Thanks

replies.author: yapdakilla81
replies.body:
with or without LLM the art process does not change with game production, you still need concept art first > blockouts > final models. or easiest these days is sketching out some ideas and using a tool to turn that into digital art. then you can use other tools like tripo3d or hyper3d to generate 3d models. 

However I must add I still extensively modified, rigged and hand animated and do final rendering for all the models using Blender3D as I have experience using 3D software. So this process still took a good few months.

replies.author: Prior-Meeting1645
replies.body: How come?  Models with vision checking their own work and fixing accordingly is so heavenly.

replies.author: yapdakilla81
replies.body: Even with AI i still get it to create really small features first and then test. So its all still within control. With smaller features easier to describe and debug issues.

replies.author: Prior-Meeting1645
replies.body: I just checked it out. Looks promising tbh. How much of the game was generated by them would you say?

replies.author: yapdakilla81
replies.body: In terms of code all based on my own architecture i designed. But I still have to run the debugger and copy paste the call stack for any crashes for them to debug. I still use other models like gemini or claude or codex to verify or work on really hard to solve issues. but for the most part chinese models code, occasional gemini/claude/codex for review.

replies.author: Useful_Use_6170
replies.body: Have you worked with 2d models? And sprite sheets that’s what I’m having trouble with in godot ?

replies.author: yapdakilla81
replies.body:
I'm not using Godot though. Custom engine using Raylib. Using prerendered 3d from blender where I still have to modify the mesh, materials, textures, rig and animate manually lol. And generated the sprite sheets from there.

Are you referring to 2d pixel art sprite sheets? I tried it once, 2d art generators didn't work so well for me back then. Not sure if it has improved now.

replies.author: Useful_Use_6170
replies.body: Yeah exactly! Well not 2d pixel art specifically more along the lines of getting sprite sheets to work unless theirs other ways to implement animations in godot I’m not aware of :(
